topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's objectives, reviewing cancer progression models and framing the lecture around the classical hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulation of Growth Factor and Inhibitory Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how genetic mutations in surface receptors and downstream cascades enable cancer cells to sustain proliferative signaling and resist growth inhibition.

topics.label: Blockade of Cellular Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how arrested differentiation maintains cells in a proliferative progenitor-like state in both hematological malignancies and colorectal carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and the dysregulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic mitochondrial proteins.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how tumors overcome the Hayflick limit and bypass stress-induced senescence through telomere maintenance and the evasion of protective DNA damage responses.

topics.label: Reprogramming of Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations generate oncometabolites that drive epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and Vascularization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how developing tumors overcome oxygen and nutrient diffusion limits by altering the balance of signaling factors to induce new blood vessel growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Genetics of Cancer Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the multi-step invasion-metastasis cascade, the seed-and-soil requirements for distant colonization, and the clonal genetics underlying metastatic dissemination.

topics.label: Concluding Remarks and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the overarching themes of cancer hallmarks, mentions recent literature extensions, and provides closing instructions for upcoming practicals.
